st: Put the beef, [[10 cups]] water, [[1 tsp]] salt and the bay leaves in a large pot. Bring to a boil, then skim off the grey foam from the top.
Reduce the heat to low, cover partly and simmer the beef until very tender.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion and carrots for [[8 minutes]] until soft, then stir in the tomato paste and cook 2 minutes more.
In a second small pan, cook the grated beets with [[1 tbsp]] oil and the vinegar over medium-low heat for 10 minutes, stirring now and then.
Lift the beef out of the pot and let it cool briefly. Shred the meat from the bones and return it to the broth.
Add the potatoes to the broth and simmer for 10 minutes. Add the cabbage and cook 5 minutes more.
Stir in the carrot and onion mixture, the beets, the garlic, [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper. Simmer 10 minutes until all the vegetables are tender.
Taste and adjust the salt. Turn off the heat, cover and let the soup rest for 15 minutes so the flavors blend.
Ladle into bowls and top each with a spoonful of sour cream and a sprinkle of dill.
Mix [[3 cups]] flour and [[1 tsp]] salt in a bowl. Add the egg and [[0.75 cup]] warm water and stir until a shaggy dough forms.
Knead the dough on a floured counter for 8 minutes until smooth and firm. Wrap it and let it rest for 30 minutes.
Combine the beef, pork, grated onion, garlic, [[1 tsp]] salt, the pepper and [[0.25 cup]] cold water. Mix well with your hands until sticky and fluffy.
Roll the dough very thin on a floured counter. Cut out circles with a small glass or cutter about 2 inches wide.
Place a small spoonful of filling in the center of each circle. Fold into a half moon and pinch the edges firmly to seal.
Curl the two corners of each half moon together and pinch them to make a little ear shape. Set on a floured tray.
Bring a large pot of well-salted water to a boil. Drop in the pelmeni in batches and stir gently so they do not stick.
Cook until they float, then 5 more minutes, so the meat is fully cooked through (pork reaches 160°F/71°C).
Lift out with a slotted spoon, toss with the melted butter and serve hot with sour cream.
Pat the beef strips dry and season with the salt and pepper. Start the noodles in boiling salted water if using them.
Heat the oil and [[1 tbsp]] butter in a large skillet over high heat. Sear the beef in two batches for 2 minutes per batch until browned, then move to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium. Melt [[1 tbsp]] butter and cook the mushrooms for 6 minutes until golden and their liquid has cooked off. Move them to the plate.
Melt the last [[1 tbsp]] butter in the skillet and cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Sprinkle in the flour and stir for 1 minute. Slowly pour in the broth, stirring, and bring to a gentle simmer.
Simmer the sauce for 5 minutes until slightly thickened. Stir in the mustard.
Lower the heat. Stir in the sour cream, then return the beef and mushrooms with their juices.
Warm everything for 2 minutes without boiling so the sour cream does not split. Taste and adjust the salt.
Serve over the noodles or potatoes with parsley on top.

ing: melted, divided, plus more for the pan
st: Whisk the egg yolks, [[1 cup]] of the milk, the sugar and salt in a large bowl.
Whisk in the flour until smooth, then add [[2 tbsp]] melted butter. Let the batter rest for 15 minutes.
Beat the egg whites until they hold soft peaks, then fold them gently into the batter.
Stir in the remaining [[0.5 cup]] milk if the batter is thicker than heavy cream. It should pour thinly.
Heat a non-stick skillet over medium heat and brush lightly with butter.
Pour in a small ladle of batter and swirl the pan to spread it thin. Cook 1 minute until the edges look set and lightly golden.
Flip and cook the other side for 30 seconds. Stack the blini on a plate, brushing each with a little melted butter.
Repeat with the remaining batter, then serve warm with sour cream, jam or smoked salmon.

ing: beef chuck or bone-in short ribs
st: Put the beef, [[8 cups]] water, bay leaves, peppercorns and [[1 tsp]] salt in a large pot. Bring to a boil and skim off any foam.
Reduce the heat, cover partly and simmer until the beef is tender.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion and carrots for 8 minutes until soft and golden.
Lift the beef out, cut the meat into bite-size pieces and return it to the broth. Discard the bones, bay leaves and any gristle.
Add the potatoes to the broth and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the cabbage, the onion and carrot mixture, garlic and [[1 tsp]] salt. Simmer for 15 minutes until the cabbage is soft.
Taste and adjust the salt. Turn off the heat and let the soup stand for 10 minutes.
Serve in bowls topped with dill and a spoonful of sour cream.
Put the potatoes and carrots in a pot, cover with cold salted water and bring to a boil. Cook until a knife slides in easily.
In a separate pot, cover the eggs with cold water, bring to a boil, then cook for 10 minutes. Cool in ice water.
Drain the potatoes and carrots and cool completely, about 20 minutes. Peel them.
Peel the eggs. Dice the potatoes, carrots and eggs into small, even cubes.
Put the diced vegetables and eggs in a large bowl with the bologna, pickles, peas and onion.
Add the mayonnaise, salt and pepper. Fold gently so the potatoes do not turn to mush.
Taste and adjust the salt. Chill for at least 30 minutes.
Sprinkle with dill and serve cold.

ing: divided, plus oil for frying or brushing
st: Stir the yeast, sugar and warm milk together and let stand 5 minutes until foamy. Add [[1 egg]], the melted butter and [[1 tsp]] salt.
Mix in the flour to make a soft dough. Knead for 8 minutes until smooth, then cover and let rise until doubled.
Meanwhile, hard-boil the second egg for 10 minutes, cool, peel and chop it.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a skillet and cook the onion and cabbage for 8 minutes until soft. Move to a bowl.
In the same skillet, cook the beef with [[0.5 tsp]] salt and the pepper until no pink remains and it reaches 160°F/71°C. Mix with the cabbage and chopped egg and cool.
Divide the risen dough into 16 pieces. Flatten each into a circle and put a spoonful of filling in the middle.
Pinch the edges tightly to seal, and set the buns seam side down on a lined baking sheet. Let them puff for 20 minutes.
To bake, heat the oven to 375°F (190°C), brush the buns with oil or beaten egg yolk and bake for 20 minutes until golden. To fry, shallow fry in oil over medium heat until deep golden on each side.
Cool for 5 minutes before eating.

ing: farmer cheese or dry cottage cheese
st: If the cheese is wet, press it in a clean towel or sieve to squeeze out extra liquid. Mash it with a fork until fairly smooth.
Mix in the egg, sugar, vanilla and salt.
Stir in [[0.5 cup]] flour until a soft, slightly sticky dough forms. Add a spoonful more flour only if it is too wet to shape.
Spread some flour on a plate. Scoop golf-ball-sized portions of dough, roll them in the flour and flatten into thick discs.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-low heat.
Fry the syrniki for 3 minutes per side until deep golden and cooked through. Keep the heat gentle so the inside sets.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm with sour cream and jam or honey.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the tomato paste and fresh tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes, stirring often.
Add the sausage and ham and cook for 5 minutes until lightly browned.
Pour in the broth, add the bay leaves and bring to a boil.
Add the pickles, pickle brine, olives, capers and pepper. Reduce the heat and simmer for 20 minutes.
Taste. It should be salty, tangy and a little sour. Add salt only if needed, as the pickles and sausage are salty.
Remove the bay leaves. Ladle into bowls and top each with a lemon slice and a spoonful of sour cream.

ing: 1 minced for filling, 1 diced for sauce
st: Cut out the core of the cabbage. Boil the whole head in salted water for 10 minutes, peeling off the softened outer leaves as they loosen with tongs.
Trim the thick rib on each leaf so it lies flat. You need about 12 leaves; chop the extra cabbage and keep it.
Mix the beef, rice, minced onion, garlic, [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper in a bowl.
Put a heaping spoonful of filling at the stem end of a leaf. Fold in the sides and roll up tightly like a small burrito. Repeat.
Heat the oil in a wide pot and cook the diced onion and carrots for 6 minutes. Stir in the tomato paste, canned tomatoes, water, [[1 tsp]] salt and bay leaves.
Spread the chopped extra cabbage in the sauce and nestle the rolls seam side down on top.
Cover and simmer gently over low heat until the rice is tender and the beef reaches 160°F/71°C.
Serve hot with sauce spooned over, sour cream and dill.
Boil the beets, potatoes and carrots in separate pots of salted water until tender when pierced. Beets take longest.
Hard-boil the eggs for 10 minutes, then cool in cold water.
Cool all vegetables completely. Peel them and grate the potatoes, carrots, beets and eggs separately on a coarse grater.
If the onion is sharp, rinse it in cold water for a minute and pat dry.
In a deep dish, spread the diced herring in an even layer and scatter the onion over it.
Layer the grated potatoes on top, then spread with [[0.3 cup]] mayonnaise. Add a pinch of salt.
Add the carrots with a little mayonnaise, then the eggs with a little mayonnaise.
Finish with the beets as the top layer and cover completely with the remaining mayonnaise.
Cover and chill for at least 4 hours so the layers set. Top with dill and cut into squares.
In a large heatproof bowl set over a pot of simmering water, melt the honey, butter and sugar together, stirring. Remove from the heat once the sugar has dissolved.
Whisk in the eggs quickly, then the baking soda. The mixture will foam. Return to the heat for 3 minutes, stirring, until it turns golden and thick.
Remove from the heat and stir in the salt and [[2 cups]] flour. Add the rest of the flour gradually until a soft dough forms, then let it cool until you can handle it.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Divide the dough into 8 equal pieces. Roll each very thin on parchment into a circle about 9 inches wide.
Bake each layer on a baking sheet for 4 minutes until golden brown. Trim neat circles while hot and keep the scraps for crumbs.
Crush the scraps in a bag with a rolling pin to make fine cake crumbs. Mix with the walnuts.
Whip the sour cream with the powdered sugar and vanilla until smooth. In another bowl, whip the heavy cream until stiff and fold it into the sour cream.
Stack the cake layers, spreading about [[0.5 cup]] cream on each. Cover the top and sides with cream and press the crumbs and walnuts all over.
Cover and chill so the layers soften and the cake can be sliced cleanly.
Cut the rye bread into cubes and bake at 350°F for 15 minutes until deeply toasted and dark brown, but not burnt.
Put the toasted bread in a large clean jar and pour in [[8 cup]] boiling water. Cover and steep for 2 hours or until cool.
Strain the liquid through a cloth, squeezing out the bread. Stir in [[0.5 cup]] sugar and [[0.5 tsp]] yeast until dissolved.
Cover loosely with a cloth and ferment at room temperature for 6 hours until bubbles appear and it smells yeasty and sour.
Stir in [[0.25 cup]] more sugar and pour into clean bottles, adding a few raisins to each. Leave 2 inches of headspace and seal.
Refrigerate for at least 24 hours before drinking. Open bottles slowly to release pressure, and chill well before serving.
nt: Toasted bread infusion, then yeast-fermented at room temperature
Best swap: gluten-free, use toasted gluten-free bread, though the flavor will be milder; for less fizz, ferment only 8 hours.

st: Roast the eggplants whole on a sheet pan at 425°F for 45 minutes, turning once, until collapsed and very soft. Cool, then scrape out the flesh and chop fine.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] sunflower oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion and bell pepper 8 minutes until soft, add tomatoes and cook 5 more until thick.
Stir in the garlic and eggplant and cook 5 minutes. Season with salt, add [[2 tbsp]] dill and chill. This is baklazhannaya ikra.
Drain the herring and cut in pieces. Toss with the red onion, [[2 tbsp]] sunflower oil and [[2 tbsp]] dill. Chill 15 minutes.
Halve the hard boiled eggs, mash the yolks with the mayonnaise and a pinch of salt, and spoon back into the whites. Top with the remaining dill.
Butter the rye slices, cut into triangles and top with radish slices and salt. Serve everything with the cornichons and the ikra.
nt: Eggplant roasted whole at 425°F then simmered with vegetables; herring and eggs are cold
Best swap: use smoked mackerel or pickled herring from the deli if you cannot find jarred; fry zucchini instead of eggplant.

st: Boil whole potatoes in salted water for 20 minutes until a knife slips in easily, then cool them completely. Peel and dice into 1/2 inch cubes.
Cook the eggs in boiling water for 10 minutes until fully hard, so the yolks are firm and safe, then cool in ice water, peel and chop.
Combine the potatoes, eggs, cucumbers, radishes, ham, scallions and dill in a large bowl. Sprinkle with the salt and mash gently so the herbs release their flavor.
Pour the cold kvass over the mixture and stir. Chill for 30 minutes if you can.
Ladle into chilled bowls and add a spoonful of sour cream to each. Taste and add salt if needed.
nt: Boiled vegetables and eggs, no cook assembly
Best swap: 3 cups kefir thinned with 2 cups cold sparkling water in place of kvass for a tangier version.
